title: Geopolitical Risk and Financial Stability

maps.tested: Counts reported per sitting: two in one recall, three in another. Consistently described as free points for anyone who actually reads the Current Issues material.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'climate risk drivers'; 'climate risk - 3 questions'; 'climate risk and inflation'; and one specific answer recall: 'climate risk question, I chose catastrophe bond as answer', indicating a risk-transfer-instrument framing. Keep physical risk drivers distinct from transition risk drivers; that split is the natural sibling swap.

vardeezReading: CI-4: Important. "Solve book-wise Current Issues questions; anything can show up."

selectors.name: Channels and policy responses
selectors.what: The two channels from geopolitical risk to asset prices and financial stability: the economic channel (trade, capital flows, supply chains, production capacity) and the market sentiment channel (uncertainty, risk aversion, lower confidence, higher volatility); and the policy responses (resilience, fiscal and monetary flexibility, deeper markets, capital and liquidity buffers).

selectors.name: Banks and nonbanks: valuations, lending, flows
selectors.what: How geopolitical risk raises market, credit and liquidity risk for banks and nonbank institutions: lower asset and collateral values and bank equity, less cross-border lending, rollover risk, and redemption pressure and fund outflows (bond funds with 10% exposure: flows about -2.3%, returns about -1%). Includes exposure to high-risk markets (8% of cross-border bank claims, 10% of liabilities, 13% of equity fund assets) and the reduction in direct exposure to Russia and Ukraine.

selectors.name: Pricing in equity and option markets
selectors.what: How investors price geopolitical risk: the sign of the risk premium (assets that lose when risk rises carry positive premiums, hedging assets low or negative), GPR betas by sector (energy and defense positive, consumer sectors negative), and the rise in downside (put) and tail (deep out-of-the-money put) premiums, tail premiums rising the most.

selectors.name: Sovereign premiums; importers versus exporters
selectors.what: Sovereign risk premiums measured by sovereign CDS spreads after major conflicts (about +180 bps in EMs, about +40 bps in AEs; weak reserves about +100 bps, weak institutions about +120 bps; safe-haven yields fall), and who gains or loses: commodity exporters gain from price spikes, importers face currency depreciation and wider spreads.

notSelected: CI-4 c (stock market responses to domestic and global events, Russia 2022 and US-China tariffs, cross-border effects) carries no shape, no Map point on geopolitical risk and no Vardeez pointer beyond a bare focus flag; the Priority Map entry listed (climate risk) concerns climate specifics that belong to other topics, so the climate-driver items it reports are deliberately left out.
